text: A database is an organized way to store and manage information. Most traditional databases, called SQL databases, use tables with rows and columns, much like a spreadsheet. To retrieve data, you write a query using a special language called SQL. Before building a database, you plan its structure through data modeling, deciding how tables connect to each other. To make searches faster, databases use indexes, which work like a book’s table of contents. However, not all data fits neatly into tables. NoSQL databases offer more flexibility by storing information as documents or key-value pairs, which is useful for large or unstructured data. Choosing between SQL and NoSQL depends on your project’s needs.
